subtype: Approach: freezing because the plan was never practised [Pitfall]
passage: The smoke alarm shrieked at 2 a.m. Pradeep sat up. He knew there was a plan; Amma had read it out once in the living room, but he had never walked it. Now he stood frozen in his doorway with tears running down his face. The words swirled: stairs, low, door... which first? "Pradeep!" His mother Preeti rushed in, took his hand and said, "Low. Follow me." They went down the stairs together and out to the gate, where neighbours were already gathering. Pradeep shivered and sobbed. Afterwards he asked whether they could really walk the way out, tomorrow, all of it.

qa.q: What time did the smoke alarm go off?
qa.a: The smoke alarm shrieked at 2 a.m.

qa.q: What was Pradeep feeling as he stood in the doorway?
qa.a: Terrified and confused, so frozen that he cried, because the plan words swirled in his head.

qa.q: What could the family do now, and why?
qa.a: They could walk the escape route together, by day and once in the dark, so the steps become movements and not only words.

qa.q: How might Preeti have felt when she found Pradeep standing there?
qa.a: Preeti was probably alarmed and protective, since she rushed in and took his hand straight away.

grounding: A child who only heard about an escape plan freezes at a real smoke alarm and needs a parent to lead him out.

subtype: Approach: freezing because the plan was never practised [Pitfall]
passage: Ayesha knew the fire rules by heart. Her school had taught them: stay low, feel the door, get out, don't go back. She could recite them faster than anyone in Class 4. Then, one night in their Bhopal flat, the smoke alarm shrieked. Smoke was drifting from the kitchen, where a pan had been forgotten on the stove. Ayesha stood in the corridor and couldn't move. Tears ran down her face. The rules were in her head, but her legs didn't know them. Her brother Zubin took her hand and pulled her to the front door while their father switched off the gas and opened the windows. Outside on the landing, Ayesha was shaking. The next weekend, the family practised the drill three times.

qa.q: What had been forgotten on the stove?
qa.a: A pan had been forgotten on the stove.

qa.q: How was Ayesha feeling as she stood in the corridor?
qa.a: She was terrified and frozen, crying, unable to turn the rules she knew into action.

qa.q: What would you change first to help Ayesha next time, and why?
qa.a: Practise the drill often at home, because doing the steps many times helps the body move even when fear takes over.

qa.q: How does the night look to Zubin?
qa.a: Zubin sees his sister frozen and acts quickly, pulling her out, so he was probably scared but focused.

grounding: It shows a child who had only heard about escape plans freezing and crying at a real smoke alarm, because knowing a rule differs from doing it under stress.

subtype: Approach: freezing because the plan was never practised [Pitfall]
passage:
"Madhuri! The alarm! Madhuri, come!"
"Harsha bhaiya... I can't..."
"What do you mean, you can't? You know the rules!"
"I know them. My legs won't go."
"Give me your hand. Low, like this. Door. Stairs. Go."
Outside, on the pavement, their mother wrapped Madhuri in a shawl. It had only been smoke from burnt toast, and Papa had already opened every window.
"I knew what to do," Madhuri sobbed. "I said it in class. But I just stood there."
"Knowing it isn't the same as doing it," Harsha said. "You've only ever heard it. Tomorrow we'll do it for real. Ten times, if you want."

qa.q: How did Madhuri feel when she said her legs wouldn't go?
qa.a: She felt frozen with fear and later upset and ashamed that she knew the rules but couldn't act.

qa.q: What else could help Madhuri besides practising at home?
qa.a: She could ask her school to include a surprise drill, so she practises moving when she isn't expecting it.

qa.q: How does the moment look to Harsha?
qa.a: Harsha is scared and impatient at first, then understanding, offering to practise with her as many times as she wants.

grounding: It shows a child freezing at a real smoke alarm because she had only heard the escape plan, and learning that knowing and doing are different.
